facts.text: The nearby Monicabrug takes its name from the Sint-Monastery Church that stood here until 1977.
facts.sourceQuote: De Monicabrug is vernoemd naar de Sint-Monicakerk die tot 1977 in de directe omgeving stond.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Monicabrug is named after the Sint-Monastery Church, which stood in the immediate vicinity until 1977.

features.name: Koekoeksvaart
features.opening: The Koekoeksvaart or Nieuwe Keizersgracht is a waterway in the Dutch city of Utrecht, running from the Biltsche Grift in the east to the Zwarte Water in the…

facts.text: A section of this canal was flattened between 1964 and 1974 to become a street.
facts.sourceQuote: Het deel van de gracht dat samenvalt met de gelijknamige straat is in de jaren 1964 tot 1974 gedempt, gelijktijdig met het oostelijk deel van het Zwarte Water.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The part of the canal that coincides with the street of the same name was flattened between 1964 and 1974, at the same time as the eastern part of the Black Water.

features.name: Oosterstroom
features.opening: The Oosterstroom is an ancient canal in the Dutch city of Utrecht.

facts.text: A roundel named Simpoel was built into the perimeter wall at its connection to Zwarte Water.
facts.sourceQuote: De aansluiting Zwarte Water - Oosterstroom was destijds aan de binnenzijde voorzien van het rondeel Simpoel aan de ommuring.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Zwarte Water - Oosterstroom connection was at the time provided on the inside with the roundel Simpoel on the perimeter wall.

features.name: Recreatieplas Strijkviertel
features.opening: The Strijkviertelplas, official name Recreatieplas Strijkviertel, is a recreational lake in the city of Utrecht.

facts.text: Sand mining operations that created the site began in 1937 under Rijkswaterstaat.
facts.sourceQuote: De plas ontstond door ontgronding ten behoeve van de zandwinning door Rijkswaterstaat, die vanaf 1937 plaatsvond.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The puddle was caused by reclamation for the purpose of sand mining by Rijkswaterstaat, which took place from 1937.

facts.text: During the 1970s and 1980s, the area received both legal and illegal waste deposits.
facts.sourceQuote: In de jaren 70 en 80 vonden legale en illegale stortingen plaats van grond, slib en bouw- en sloopafval.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In the 1970s and 1980s, legal and illegal deposits of soil, sludge and construction and demolition waste took place.

facts.text: Engineers covered the bottom with at least one meter of sand plus clay and peat.
facts.sourceQuote: De bodem werd door Rijkswaterstaat afgedekt door een laag zand van minimaal een meter, en in de zuidoostelijke hoek klei en veen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The bottom was covered by Rijkswaterstaat with a layer of sand of at least one meter, and in the southeastern corner clay and peat.

facts.text: The pond reaches a maximum depth of 8.5 meters.
facts.sourceQuote: De diepte van de plas is maximaal 8,5 meter.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The depth of the pond is a maximum of 8.5 meters.

facts.text: The annual Lief Festival is held at this location.
facts.sourceQuote: Jaarlijks vindt in Strijkviertel het Lief Festival plaats.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Lief Festival takes place annually in Strijkviertel.

features.name: Drift
features.opening: The Drift is a canal and street in the city center of the Dutch city of Utrecht.

facts.text: The name Drift originally described a road where farmers drove their cattle to the city.
facts.sourceQuote: De benaming drift staat oorspronkelijk voor een weg waarlangs de boeren hun vee naar Utrecht dreven.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The name drift originally stood for a road along which the farmers drove their cattle to Utrecht.

facts.text: Houses along the canal are accessed via seven private bridges because no street exists on the west side.
facts.sourceQuote: Net als de Kromme Nieuwegracht heeft de Drift daardoor aan de westzijde geen straat. De huizen zijn er bereikbaar door middel van zeven particuliere bruggen over de gracht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Like the Kromme Nieuwegracht, the Drift therefore has no street on the west side. The houses are accessible by means of seven private bridges over the canal.

features.name: Vecht
features.opening: The Weerdsluis is a floodgate with pointed doors in the Dutch city of Utrecht.

facts.text: In the 18th and 19th centuries, women and children hand-pulled ships through because draft horses were banned inside the city walls.
facts.sourceQuote: Bij de Weerdsluis bevonden zich in de 18e en 19e eeuw veel mensen, waaronder vrouwen en kinderen, die zich beschikbaar stelden om de schepen door de Utrechtse singels en grachten met menskracht te trekken, dit omdat de stad binnen haar muren het gebruik van trekpaarden verboden had.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: At the Weerdsluis, many people, including women and children, were present in the 18th and 19th centuries who volunteered to pull the ships through the Utrecht canals and singels by hand, this because the city had banned the use of draft horses within its walls.

features.name: Biltsche Grift
features.opening: The Biltsche Grift is a waterway in the Dutch province of Utrecht.

facts.text: From 1873 to the 1920s, a bulge in the canal served as an open-air public bathing resort.
facts.sourceQuote: Vanaf 1873 tot het eind van de jaren 20 in de 20e eeuw was er een uitstulping in de Biltsche Grift ter hoogte van de Utrechtse Grasstraat. De uitstulping werd gebruikt als openbare badplaats in de openlucht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: From 1873 until the end of the 1920s in the 20th century, there was an outcropping in the Biltsche Grift near Utrechtse Grasstraat. The bulge was used as an open-air public bathing resort.

facts.text: A now abolished water board in the area was named after this waterway.
facts.sourceQuote: In bredere zin werd een, inmiddels opgeheven, waterschap in het gebied van de vaart vernoemd naar de waterweg.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In a broader sense, a now abolished water board in the area of the canal was named after the waterway.

features.name: Zwarte Water
features.opening: The Zwarte Water is an ancient watercourse in the Dutch city of Utrecht that flows into the Vecht River.

facts.text: The name Zwarte Water comes from the dark peat water that originally flowed through it.
facts.sourceQuote: Deze watergang, die de naam Zwarte Water kreeg vanwege het donkere veenwater, kwam ter hoogte van de Nieuwe Keizersgracht uit op de Oude Vecht.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: This watercourse, which was named Zwarte Water because of the dark peat water, flowed into the Oude Vecht near the Nieuwe Keizersgracht.

facts.text: Work to fill in sections of the canal began in 1964 and was completed by draining the final part in 1974.
facts.sourceQuote: Een aanzienlijk deel (van Merelstraat tot Kardinaal de Jongweg) werd in de jaren 1964 tot 1974 gedempt na acties waartoe de Utrechtse Muurkrant felle oproepen deed. In 1964 werd begonnen met het dempen van het deel tussen Draaiweg en Kardinaal de Jongweg, in 1974 werd het proces voltooid met het droogleggen van het stuk tussen Merelstraat en Draaiweg.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: A significant part (from Merelstraat to Kardinaal de Jongweg) was silenced in the years 1964 to 1974 after actions to which the Utrechtse Muurkrant made strong appeals. In 1964, work began to fill in the section between Draaiweg and Kardinaal de Jongweg, and in 1974, the process was completed by draining the section between Merelstraat and Draaiweg.

features.name: Vaartsche Rijn
features.opening: The Vaartse Rijn is a canal connecting the city of Utrecht with Nieuwegein and the Lek river in the Dutch province of Utrecht.

facts.text: Floris V ordered a new stretch built in 1285 to restore the connection to the Lek.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1285 Floris V, Count of Holland dammed the Hollandse IJssel connection between the Lek and the Hollandse IJssel. In order to maintain the connection between the Utrecht and the Lek, Floris ordered the construction of a new stretch of the Vaartse Rijn (the "Nieuwe Vaart"), to meet the Lek directly at Vreeswijk.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1285 Floris V, Count of Holland dammed the Hollandse IJssel connection between the Lek and the Hollandse IJssel. In order to maintain the connection between the Utrecht and the Lek, Floris ordered the construction of a new stretch of the Vaartse Rijn (the "Nieuwe Vaart"), to meet the Lek directly at Vreeswijk.

facts.text: A lock at Vreeswijk was installed in 1373 after the canal was deepened.
facts.sourceQuote: In 1373 the Vaartse Rijn was deepened, and a lock installed at Vreeswijk.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In 1373 the Vaartse Rijn was deepened, and a lock installed at Vreeswijk.

features.name: Nedereindse Plas
features.opening: The Nedereindse Plas is a recreational area in the province of Utrecht in the Netherlands, near Nieuwegein.

facts.text: Waste dumping at the site officially ceased in 1992.
facts.sourceQuote: De stortactiviteiten zijn in 1992 beëindigd.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The deposit activities were discontinued in 1992.

facts.text: Illegal dumps included lightly radioactive hospital waste and welding plasma.
facts.sourceQuote: Naast legaal afval is er ook veel illegaal afval gestort, waaronder licht radioactief ziekenhuisafval, lasplasma en vaten met onbekende chemische inhoud.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In addition to legal waste, there has also been a lot of illegal waste dumped, including lightly radioactive hospital waste, welding plasma and containers with unknown chemical contents.

facts.text: Containers holding unknown chemical contents were also illegally discarded there.
facts.sourceQuote: Naast legaal afval is er ook veel illegaal afval gestort, waaronder licht radioactief ziekenhuisafval, lasplasma en vaten met onbekende chemische inhoud.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In addition to legal waste, there has also been a lot of illegal waste dumped, including lightly radioactive hospital waste, welding plasma and containers with unknown chemical contents.

features.name: Kromme Nieuwegracht
features.opening: The Kromme Nieuwegracht is a canal in the center of the Dutch city of Utrecht.

facts.text: The northern half likely followed the original Rhine arm until around 1000 AD.
facts.sourceQuote: Het is dan ook zeer waarschijnlijk dat de noordelijke helft van de Kromme Nieuwegracht (tussen Hieronymusplantsoen en Jansdam) tot circa 1000 na Chr. het tracé volgde van de originele Rijnarm.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It is therefore very likely that the northern half of the Kromme Nieuwegracht (between Hieronymusplantsoen and Jansdam) followed the course of the original Rhine arm until around 1000 AD.

facts.text: The Pietersbrug stands as the sole public bridge crossing this narrow canal.
facts.sourceQuote: De enige openbare brug over de Kromme Nieuwegracht is de Pietersbrug, die toegang geeft tot de Pieterstraat.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The only public bridge over the Kromme Nieuwegracht is the Pietersbrug, which provides access to Pieterstraat.

facts.text: A reconstruction from around 1897 depicted the site as it appeared circa 1100.
facts.sourceQuote: In een reconstructie uit ca. 1897 van de situatie rond het jaar 1100 werd deze benoemd als de Ringsloot van St.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: In a reconstruction from approx. 1897 from the situation around the year 1100 this was named the Ringsloot of St.

facts.text: The Brothers of the Common Life established a convent and school here in 1474.
facts.sourceQuote: Pieter In 1474 stichtten Broeders van het Gemene Leven aan de gracht het Hieronymusconvent met daaraan verbonden de Hiëronymusschool die tot de 19e eeuw daar gevestigd zou blijven.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Pieter In 1474, Brothers of the Common Life founded the Hieronymus Convent on the canal, with the Hieronymus School attached to it, which would remain there until the 19th century.

features.name: Leidse Rijn
features.opening: The Leidse Rijn (Dutch for "Leiden's Rhine") is a canal in the province of Utrecht, Netherlands.

facts.text: A new shortcut named Leidse Rijn was dug between 1662 and 1665 under Mayor Hendrick Moreelse.
facts.sourceQuote: Under the expansion plans of the Utrecht city mayor Hendrick Moreelse in 1662-1665 a new shortcut was dug, the Leidse Rijn, connecting to where the Oude Rijn canal made a curve to the northeast.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Under the expansion plans of the Utrecht city mayor Hendrick Moreelse in 1662-1665 a new shortcut was dug, the Leidse Rijn, connecting to where the Oude Rijn canal made a curve to the northeast.

facts.text: Nobleman Everard Meyster built the Oog in Al estate where the canal connected to the old river.
facts.sourceQuote: At the place where the new canal connected to the Oude Rijn the nobleman Everard Meyster built an estate called Oog in Al.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: At the place where the new canal connected to the Oude Rijn the nobleman Everard Meyster built an estate called Oog in Al.

facts.text: The name Leidse Rijn eventually covered the entire section from Utrecht to Harmelen.
facts.sourceQuote: Eventually the name Leidse Rijn came to be used for the whole section Utrecht-Harmelen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Eventually the name Leidse Rijn came to be used for the whole section Utrecht-Harmelen.

facts.text: Digging began in the Middle Ages after the old meandering Rhine course silted up.
facts.sourceQuote: It was dug since the Middle Ages when the meandering old Rhine course silted up.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: It was dug since the Middle Ages when the meandering old Rhine course silted up.

facts.text: The waterway ends in Harmelen where it joins the Oude Rijn to flow toward Katwijk aan Zee.
facts.sourceQuote: The canal ends in Harmelen. There it connects to the Oude Rijn, which eventually flows into the North Sea at Katwijk aan Zee.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The canal ends in Harmelen. There it connects to the Oude Rijn, which eventually flows into the North Sea at Katwijk aan Zee.

features.name: Haarrijnse Plas
features.opening: The Haarrijnseplas is a sand mining pond in the Dutch municipality of Utrecht near the A2 motorway.

facts.text: Thirteen million cubic meters of sand were removed from this pit.
facts.sourceQuote: Uit dit zandgat is 13 miljoen m³ zand is gewonnen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: 13 million m³ of sand has been extracted from this sand pit.

facts.text: A road crossing the water connects Maarssen with Vleuten.
facts.sourceQuote: De plas wordt doorsneden door de Maarssenseweg, de weg tussen Maarssen en Themaat (Vleuten).
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The pond is crossed by the Maarssenseweg, the road between Maarssen and Themaat (Vleuten).

features.name: Plompetorengracht
features.opening: The Plompetorengracht is a short canal and street in the city center of Utrecht.

facts.text: The canal was dug in 1392 to improve drainage before new buildings were constructed.
facts.sourceQuote: De Plompetorengracht werd in 1392 samen met de Nieuwegracht, de Kromme Nieuwegracht en de Drift gerealiseerd, waarschijnlijk om de ontwatering van het gebied te verbeteren als voorbereiding op de aanleg van de bebouwing.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: The Plompetorengracht was realized in 1392 together with the Nieuwegracht, the Kromme Nieuwegracht and the Drift, probably to improve the drainage of the area as a preparation for the construction of the buildings.

facts.text: A guild of marching musicians used the tower as a night guard post and rented part of it as a prison.
facts.sourceQuote: Aan de noordelijke uitmonding van dit grachtstelsel door de stadsmuur in de verdedigingsgracht (de Weerdsingel), bevond zich de Plompetoren die het gilde der marslieden (marktkooplieden) 's nachts als bewaker had en door hun deels werd verhuurd als gevangenis.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: At the northern outlet of this canal system through the city wall into the defensive moat (the Weerdsingel), there was the Plompetoren, which the guild of marching musicians (market vendors) had as a guard at night and was partly rented out as a prison by them.

facts.text: Unlike neighboring canals, this stretch lacks boathouses but features boat sheds leading directly to the water.
facts.sourceQuote: Werven ontbreken hier, wel is er een aantal werfkelders die rechtstreeks op het water uitkomen.
facts.sourceQuoteEnglish: Boathouses are missing here, but there are a number of boat sheds that lead directly to the water.
